site.name: Saint Oswald's Minster & Medieval Priory
site.description: The historic minster of Saint Oswald of Northumbria founded by Æthelflæd of Mercia in the 10th century, later an Augustinian priory. Now ruinous but a site of much religious and historic importance.

osmTags.name: Saint Oswald's Minster & Medieval Priory
osmTags.description: The historic minster of Saint Oswald of Northumbria founded by Æthelflæd of Mercia in the 10th century, later an Augustinian priory. Now ruinous but a site of much religious and historic importance.

osmTags.inscription: In this building which incorporates a 12C abbot's lodging lived William Laud, Dean of Gloucester 1616-21, later to be Archbishop of Canterbury, accused of treason and beheaded on Tower Hill

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Mapped outline, terrain and present-day surroundings from open data. No historic reconstruction.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
